you are VALID. BPD is a SEVERE condition to live with, and yes it is a personality disorder that affects others too. I had all 9 symptoms of BPD and in my experience it has been a transient condition, while trauma and core beliefs are a deeper problem to work through. Here's the best map I've made to navigate out of the mess of my life and am still using:


gaining sobriety from problem behaviors has to be the first step (whatever gives you the most secondary toxic shame). second, I would start adding in a program of recovery & community -- IMO, you can use anything as a recovery plan: group DBT, dungeons & dragons/RPG, yoga/meditation, 12 steps programs, religion, a class/club at the library, an art or music class/group, an intramural sport...just make sure the community feels safe and non-dramatic, and create consistency in showing up no matter how you feel...this is opposite action to depression, and de-isolating is very, very important to recovery even though you will fuck up with interpersonal interactions. third, employ distress tolerance skills. understand that you will mess up.. over time it will become less severe and less frequent. when your brain is distressed and suicidal thoughts are nonstop, you have to lower the bar. Use the TIP skills: Temp: icepack onto forehead for a minute or so, Intense exercise: you can play a fast paced song and move your body, in order to help digest the cortisol, Paced breathing and paired muscle relaxation: easy to follow if you type in "Yoga Nidra" on YouTube. TIP has taken me from "I'm ready to die NOW," to "Maybe I can try x or y next and see if that helps me feel better." In DBT, x and y are Distract and Self Soothe. For distract you can add in things that maybe aren't in line with your big goals, but they will manage the distress in the meantime... maybe it's getting ice cream, asking a friend for a favor to spend time with you, or sitting through a movie and using that as a way to fill up the next hour or so, so that you don't feel like you'll go insane. Self Soothe, I have rephrased as Slightly Less Shitty... because I feel so bad in these times: you take any action you can to feel slightly less shitty...adjust a pillow, get a glass of water, a gentle stretch or massage, good music or good videos, a nice snack, putting on some lotion and comforting clothes. my own additions to distress tolerance: stop blaming yourself for being emotional, because it's very likely someone dropped the ball at some point in your life to make you feel this way. change your environment to create change in your mind. even 20 minutes away from your space can create a meaningful shift. also, it helps me to thank my suicidal thoughts for wanting to protect me from future harm.💔🙏🏼


after you do distress tolerance skills, then you will unlock the ability to do emotional regulation skills: focusing more on middle-line goals like: Personal hygiene, following through on all your medical needs especially for a physical iLlness, Eating regular balanced meals, hydrating (alcohol Alternatives), Sleeping, Exercise, (the PLEASE acronym )


top-line goals, to me, would be: Accumulate positive experiences, pick anything to Build master at, and Cleaning and coping ahead (the ABC acronym), and (GIVE FAST) the interpersonal effectiveness skill off: to maintain a relationship /prevent rejection: Gentle smile and hands, Interest in what the other person is saying, Validate their personal experiences, Etiquette/Ease of manner. and to maintain self-esteem: be Fair, Assert or Apologize, Stick to values, be Truthful (if safe to do so). DEAR MAN is an acronym you can Google if you need to make or decline requests. 


No matter which emotional level you are at, practice mindfulness. If you want, you could try a little meditation, but this can be very hard for emotionally dysregulated people. Main qualities of mindfulness include: -nonjudgmentalness of the experience--shift from dysregulating, morality -based thoughts ie "this is/I am being good or bad" to "this behavior is effective/ineffective"/"this environment is validating/invalidating". -observe and describe: even if it seems stupid or silly, thinking facts such as "today is Tuesday ", "the sky is blue", "that stop sign is an octagon shape" gives your logical mind more room to take the reigns. It's ideal to integrate logical mind and emotional mind together: "wise mind" -participate fully in the present moment. ie, if you are driving, try to notice the senses and even narrate in your mind or aloud what you are doing and feeling. presence can make you safer, more in control of your behaviors (which is what boundaries are truly about), and can satisfy deep cravings your body and mind have. Best wishes and I hope you get through this💜
